title: The effects of AI-based visual instruction on the reading comprehension of students with dyslexia in Saudi Arabia: a single-case experimental study
extended_summary:
The paper addresses persistent reading comprehension difficulties among students with dyslexia, particularly in Arabic-language educational contexts where linguistic and orthographic features may intensify reading challenges. The authors examine whether generative AI can provide individualized visual instructional support that improves comprehension for students who had not responded adequately to traditional approaches.

The intervention used ChatGPT/GPT-4 to generate visual explanations and illustrative supports aligned with Grade 4 Arabic language textbook passages. Students received one-to-one guided reading sessions in which AI-generated visuals were connected to the reading text, followed by five-question comprehension quizzes assessing skills such as literal understanding, inference, main idea identification, detail recognition, and information synthesis.

The study was conducted in a public elementary school in Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, with three male fourth-grade students aged 9–11 diagnosed with dyslexia. A single-case experimental multiple-probe design across participants was used over 32 weeks, with baseline, intervention, and maintenance phases. Procedural fidelity was monitored and reported as very high.

All three students began with low, stable baseline comprehension performance and improved after the GenAI-supported visual instruction was introduced. Two students showed immediate level changes and the third showed a gradual accelerating trend, with all reaching or maintaining mastery-level performance during treatment and maintenance probes. The authors conclude that GenAI-based visual instruction shows preliminary promise for supporting reading comprehension among elementary students with dyslexia, while noting the need for larger and more generalizable research.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: ChatGPT is an OpenAI generative AI chatbot; in this study, GPT-4 was used to generate visual explanations and illustrative instructional materials aligned with Arabic reading passages.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate visual explanations and illustrative materials for Grade 4 Arabic reading passages to support reading comprehension instruction for students with dyslexia.

findings.finding_summary: In a single-case multiple-probe study with three male Grade 4 students with dyslexia (n=3), ChatGPT-generated visual instruction was associated with improved reading comprehension quiz performance. Baseline scores were low and stable at 0%–10%; during intervention, all participants reached the mastery criterion of at least 80% across three consecutive sessions, and maintenance probes showed sustained performance at or above mastery.
findings.measure: Five-question reading comprehension quizzes scored as percentage correct, based on Grade 4 Arabic textbook passages

quality_tier_rationale: This was a single-case experimental study using a multiple-probe across participants design with stable baselines, staggered intervention introduction, procedural fidelity checks, and interobserver agreement. The evidence is limited by the very small sample (n=3), one school setting, and lack of randomized group comparison.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reported large positive changes in reading comprehension quiz performance for all three participants, from baseline scores of 0%–10% to sustained mastery-level performance of 80%–90%. No standardized effect size was reported, but visual analysis indicated a strong functional relation, minimal or no phase overlap, and durable effects.
